options.name: api_host
options.description: The hostname or IP address of the pfSense device.

options.name: api_key
options.description: An API key to use for authentication.

options.name: api_password
options.description: The password to authenticate with the pfSense API.

options.name: api_port
options.description: The port number of the pfSense API.

options.name: api_protocol
options.description: The protocol to use when connecting to the pfSense API.

options.name: api_username
options.description: The username to authenticate with the pfSense API.

options.name: descr
options.description: A description for the outbound NAT mapping.

options.name: destination
options.description: The destination network this rule should match. Valid value options are: an existing interface, a subnet CIDR, an existing alias, `any`, `pppoe`. The context of this address can be inverted by prefixing the value with `!`. For interface values, the `:ip` modifier can be appended to the value to use the interface's IP address instead of its entire subnet.

options.name: destination_port
options.description: The destination port this rule should match. Valid options are: a TCP/UDP port number, a TCP/UDP port range separated by `:`, an existing port type firewall alias

options.name: disabled
options.description: Disable this outbound NAT rule.

options.name: interface
options.description: The interface on which traffic is matched as it exits the firewall. In most cases this is a WAN-type or another externally-connected interface.

options.name: lookup_fields
options.description: The list of fields to use when looking up existing resources. This should be a list of field names that uniquely identify a resource.

options.name: nat_port
options.description: The external source port or port range used for rewriting the original source port on connections matching the rule. Valid options are: a TCP/UDP port number, a TCP/UDP port range separated by `:`

options.name: nonat
options.description: Do not NAT traffic matching this rule.

options.name: nosync
options.description: Do not sync this rule to HA peers.

options.name: poolopts
options.description: The pool option used to load balance external IP mapping when `target` is set to a subnet or alias of many addresses. Set to `null` to revert to the system default.

options.name: protocol
options.description: The protocol this rule should match. Use `null` for any protocol.

options.name: source
options.description: The source network this rule should match. Valid value options are: an existing interface, a subnet CIDR, an existing alias, `any`, `(self)`, `pppoe`. The context of this address can be inverted by prefixing the value with `!`. For interface values, the `:ip` modifier can be appended to the value to use the interface's IP address instead of its entire subnet.

options.name: source_hash_key
options.description: The key that is fed to the hashing algorithm in hex format. This must be a 16 byte (32 character) hex string prefixed with `0x`. If a value is not provided, one will automatically be generated

options.name: source_port
options.description: The source port this rule should match. Valid options are: a TCP/UDP port number, a TCP/UDP port range separated by `:`, an existing port type firewall alias

options.name: state
options.description: Whether the resource should be present or absent.

options.name: static_nat_port
options.description: Do not rewrite source port for traffic matching this rule.

options.name: target
options.description: The target network traffic matching this rule should be translated to. Valid value options are: an IP address, an existing alias. For interface values, the `:ip` modifier can be appended to the value to use the interface's IP address instead of its entire subnet.

options.name: target_subnet
options.description: The subnet bits for the assigned `target`. This field is only applicable if `target` is set to an IP address. This has no affect for alias or interface `targets`.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Whether to validate SSL certificates when connecting to the API.
